title: Anne and the chatterbox essays
body:
Read the following summary of an episode from Anne's diary entry of 20 June 1942 and answer the questions.

Anne's maths teacher, Mr Keesing, was annoyed with her for a long time because she talked so much in class. After several warnings he gave her extra homework: a three-page essay on 'A Chatterbox'. That evening, chewing the tip of her fountain pen, Anne decided that the trick was not to ramble on but to find convincing arguments for the necessity of talking. When she talked through the next lesson too, he set a second essay, 'An Incorrigible Chatterbox'. Some lessons later he had had enough and ordered a third, 'Quack, Quack, Quack, Said Mistress Chatterbox'. The class roared. With help from her friend Sanne, who was good at poetry, Anne wrote the essay in verse, about a mother duck, a father swan and three ducklings who were bitten to death by their father because they quacked too much. Mr Keesing took the joke the right way, read the poem to several classes, and from then on Anne was allowed to talk without being given extra homework.
